uncited: It differs from its parent [Training Ray Shuffling](5446-training-ray-shuffling.md) by performing the actual data movement on the GPU via a custom kernel, whereas the parent handles initialization and transfer of indices.
It addresses the need to reorder rays for better cache locality or load balancing during differentiable volume rendering optimization.

- Source ray arrays (`src`) containing: `cameraCenterX_Device`, `cameraCenterY_Device`, `cameraCenterZ_Device`, `directionX_Device`, `directionY_Device`, `directionZ_Device`, `near_t_Device`, `far_t_Device`, `gtMask_Device`, and color channels (`gtGray_Device` if grayscale, else `gtRed_Device`, `gtGreen_Device`, `gtBlue_Device`).
- Destination ray arrays (`dest`) with identical layout.
- Destination ray arrays (`dest`) with rays reordered according to `shuffledIndexArray`.
Rays are stored in Structure of Arrays (SoA) format on the GPU.
Each attribute is a separate device array of size `totalRays`.
Host function allocates destination memory for ray attributes.
Host function calls `ShuffleRank` (implementation not provided in source) to generate `shuffledIndexArray`.
Host function copies `shuffledIndexArray` to GPU.
Host function launches the `shuffleToNewGroup` kernel with grid/block dimensions sized to `src.totalRays`.
Each thread computes its global `destRayIndex`.
If `destRayIndex < src.totalRays`, the thread reads the source index from `shuffledIndexArray[destRayIndex]`.
The thread copies all ray attributes from the source arrays to the destination arrays using the mapped source index.
If `src.graylized` is true, copy `gtGray_Device`; otherwise, copy `gtRed_Device`, `gtGreen_Device`, and `gtBlue_Device`.
- Precision issues may arise if `shuffledIndexArray` contains out-of-bounds indices.
- The kernel assumes `src` and `dest` have the same `totalRays` count.
- **Time Complexity**: O(N) where N is the number of rays, as each ray is copied once.
- **Memory Complexity**: O(N) for the destination arrays and the index array.
- **When to use**: When ray order affects training stability or performance.
- **When not to use**: When memory is constrained or ray order is not critical.
It is used in differentiable volume rendering optimization loops to manage ray data efficiently.
